notes.A: Street-level view shows the clock and both entrances, but the steep angle foreshortens the sign.
notes.B: The corner storefront and distant towers dominate while the station disappears behind a stone wall.
notes.C: The ornate building and broad plaza push the station entrances to the right edge.
notes.D: Both gables, the clock, and the brick alley establish the setting, but the name is clipped.
notes.E: The whole frontage reads clearly, though the elevated view makes the entrances feel small.
notes.F: The lamps lead toward the station, but the dark alley divides attention and the clock is clipped.
notes.G: Close framing shows the gables and lamps well, but crops the clock and station name.
notes.H: Pavement and lamps lead into the nearest doorway, but the clock and most lettering vanish.

station_front.best: E fits the full station name, clock, both entrances, and lamplit pavement into one view, with the brick alley alongside.
station_front.lacks: The clock and lettering identify the station, but two similar dark entrances give the forecourt no clear point of arrival.
station_front.fix: Turn the main doorway into a broad, warmly lit entrance with the ticket hall visible from the street.

blind_name.name: Railway station entrance
blind_name.why: A round clock crowns the stone frontage, with recessed entrances and streetlamps along the cobbled pavement.
blind_name.odd: The far end of the alley is hard to make out.
